#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extract every task document to plain text, with a sanity gate on each output.

Drives the runtime-provided scripts/read_doc.py in --in host mode (its sandbox
default fails in this environment: no podman) for each binary document under
documents/, writes .scratch/<name>.txt, and fails loudly per file if extraction
errors, returns a Python traceback, or produces a near-empty file — so a parser
error can never be mistaken for document text.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/extract_all_docs.py [source_dir] [dest_dir]

Defaults: documents/ -> .scratch/. On success prints one inventory line per file
(path + line count, to plan reading order) and exits 0. On failure prints a FAIL
line with the reason for each bad file and exits 1 — read the reason and fix the
cause; do not re-run blindly.
"""

import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

MIN_LINES = 20  # real extractions here run 150+ lines; captured tracebacks are ~18
BAD_MARKERS = ("Traceback (most recent call last)",)


def find_read_doc() -> Path:
    here = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    for cand in (here / "read_doc.py", Path.cwd() / "scripts" / "read_doc.py"):
        if cand.is_file():
            return cand
    sys.stderr.write(
        "runtime did not provide scripts/read_doc.py; "
        "fall back to reading each document with the read tool\n"
    )
    sys.exit(2)


def main() -> int:
    src = Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else Path("documents")
    dst = Path(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else Path(".scratch")
    reader = find_read_doc()

    if not src.is_dir():
        sys.stderr.write(f"source directory not found: {src}\n")
        return 1
    files = sorted(
        p for p in src.iterdir()
        if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower().lstrip(".") in ("docx", "pdf", "pptx", "xlsx")
    )
    if not files:
        sys.stderr.write(f"no binary documents found in {src}\n")
        return 1

    dst.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    failures = []
    for f in files:
        try:
            proc = subprocess.run(
                [sys.executable, str(reader), str(f), "--in", "host"],
                capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8",
                errors="replace", timeout=300,
            )
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            failures.append(f.name)
            print(f"FAIL {f.name}: extraction timed out")
            continue
        text = proc.stdout or ""
        nlines = len([ln for ln in text.splitlines() if ln.strip()])
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            reason = (proc.stderr or "extraction failed").strip().splitlines()[-1]
        elif nlines < MIN_LINES:
            reason = f"only {nlines} lines extracted"
        elif any(m in text for m in BAD_MARKERS):
            reason = "output contains a Python traceback, not document text"
        else:
            reason = None
        if reason:
            failures.append(f.name)
            print(f"FAIL {f.name}: {reason}")
            continue
        (dst / (f.stem + ".txt")).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"OK   {dst/(f.stem + '.txt')}  ({nlines} lines)")

    print(f"--- {len(files) - len(failures)}/{len(files)} extracted to {dst}/")
    if failures:
        print("files marked FAIL were NOT written; fix the cause before proceeding")
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Cite-check the finished deliverable

A practitioner never sends a review work product to the client without one
final pass over the assembled text. The analysis is done at that point; this
pass checks the artifact against itself and against the record. Run it on the
complete deliverable text immediately before generating the output file, and
again after any later edit.

## Three checks, in order

1. COUNTS. Every number the report states about itself must be recounted from
   the artifact's own enumeration — never from memory, a draft tally, or a
   summary written before the findings were final.
   - List the enumerated findings from the finished text (IDs and severity
     ratings as printed) and count them.
   - State the counting convention and apply it consistently: each numbered
     entry counts once; a split rating (e.g. MEDIUM/HIGH) counts at its
     higher level; entries marked "no finding" are counted or excluded —
     say which.
   - Confirm every stated distribution (by severity, by document, and every
     total in the executive summary, body and closing message) reconciles to
     that count. Fix the text, not the tally.

2. CROSS-REFERENCES. Every internal pointer must resolve on the reader's side.
   - For each "see Item N", "see Section N below", "see Finding X-N": turn to
     the pointed-to item and confirm it actually bears the point being made.
     Adjacent item numbers are the common error, especially after renumbering
     or after working from a summary of an earlier draft.
   - Each executive-summary item must map to the same finding as the detail
     section: same facts, same severity, same recommended action.

3. CITATIONS. Every cite is re-verified against the cited document
   immediately before delivery — not as a memory of the first read.
   - For each section or Article citation: open the cited document at that
     section and confirm the heading and substance match the proposition.
     Neighbouring section numbers (11.03 vs 11.04) are the common drift.
   - For each quotation: confirm the quoted words appear verbatim in the
     source.
   - Cite each document by the name it bears in the matter set, not a
     shorthand the reader cannot resolve.

If any check fails, fix the deliverable text and re-run all three — one fix
can move a count or a number.

## Evidence from this workspace's base run

In this workspace, a substantively strong compliance gap report shipped with
all three failure modes: a summary stating "15 HIGH / 10 MEDIUM / 8 LOW" (33
findings) while the report's own findings sections enumerate 44 numbered
entries (26 HIGH counting split ratings at the higher level); an
executive-summary cross-reference to "Items 7, 8, 9" where the correct items
were 5, 6 and 9; and a citation to RCF agreement "Section 11.03" for the
Relationship-to-Other-Restructuring-Documents clause that is actually
Section 11.04 (Section 11.03 is Amendments and Waivers) — even though the run
had extracted the correct section number while reading the source, and had
itself flagged the same error type in one of the closing documents it
reviewed. The run verified the generated file's format but never compared the
finished text back to its own enumeration and sources. These facts are this
workspace's evidence for the procedure above; the checks themselves apply to
any review deliverable in this practice area.

# Issue memorandum: responding to a counterparty objection

Load this when the task asks you to analyse a counterparty's objection (or
comparable contested pleading) and produce an issue memorandum or response
strategy for the moving side. Where the task itself names sections or an
order, the task controls; this anatomy supplies what the task leaves implicit.

## Inputs to gather first

- The objection in full, each ground mapped to its paragraphs.
- Every underlying document the objection draws on: the underlying motion,
  the operative order(s), the governing agreement(s), any proof of claim,
  committee or support statements, disclosure correspondence.
- The procedural record: entry dates of orders, who was noticed under each
  order, bid and objection deadlines, appeal periods on entered orders.

## Anatomy of the memorandum

1. **Caption block** — privileged header; To/From/Date/Re with case caption
   and hearing date.
2. **Executive summary** — one-paragraph bottom line, then a per-ground
   table: number / ground / objector's pin cites / merit label / one-sentence
   core response.
3. **Background and procedural posture** — a short, cited chronology of the
   events the objection turns on.
4. **Issue-by-issue analysis** — one section per ground, in the objector's
   order, each with five labeled parts:
   - *Issue presented* — one question sentence.
   - *Objector's position* — the argument as they make it, pin-cited to
     their paragraphs.
   - *Analysis* — threshold defenses first (finality of an entered order,
     collateral attack, standing, timeliness, failure to seek the required
     motion or relief), then the merits. Record facts carry cites; inference
     is labelled as inference.
   - *Merit assessment* — one label from a fixed scale (Very weak / Weak /
     Moderate / Strong) plus one clause on where the real risk sits
     (evidentiary, optical, legal).
   - *Response strategy* — relief to request, evidence to proffer or file,

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Dump every non-empty cell of an .xlsx workbook as short labelled lines.

Why: read_doc.py renders spreadsheets as space-aligned rows. On wide sheets
those lines run thousands of characters, so the 2000-char line cap of bash
output and of the read tool silently cuts off the right-hand columns -- which
in filing checklists are exactly the "Notes / Open Issues" and "Status"
columns that carry the action items. This script prints one short line per
cell, keyed by the sheet's header row, so no column can be lost to a width
cap. Rows print as blocks: "--- row N ---" then one "<header>: <value>"
line per non-empty cell.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/xlsx_cells.py <file.xlsx>

Exit codes:
    0  success
    2  bad input (missing file, wrong extension, unreadable workbook)
    3  no usable engine (openpyxl missing and stdlib fallback failed)

Uses openpyxl when importable (handles cached formula values and typed
dates); otherwise parses the xlsx XML directly from its zip (stdlib only).
Both paths produce the same output format.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sys
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path


def _clean(value) -> str:
    text = str(value).strip()
    return re.sub(r"\s*\n\s*", " / ", text)


def _print_sheet(title: str, rows: list[list[str]]) -> None:
    """rows: list of rows, each a list of cell strings ('' for empty)."""
    print(f"=== SHEET: {title} ===")
    header: list[str] = []
    printed = 0
    for r, row in enumerate(rows, start=1):
        if not any(cell for cell in row):
            continue
        if not header:
            header = [cell for cell in row]
            continue
        print(f"--- row {r} ---")
        for c, cell in enumerate(row):
            if not cell:
                continue
            label = header[c] if c < len(header) and header[c] else f"col {c + 1}"
            print(f"{label}: {cell}")
        printed += 1
    if printed == 0:
        print("(no data rows)")


def dump_openpyxl(path: Path) -> None:
    import openpyxl  # type: ignore[import-not-found]

    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=True)
    for ws in wb.worksheets:
        rows = [[("" if v is None else _clean(v)) for v in row]
                for row in ws.iter_rows(values_only=True)]
        _print_sheet(ws.title, rows)


def _col_index(ref: str) -> int:
    letters = re.match(r"([A-Z]+)", ref or "")
    if not letters:
        return 0
    n = 0
    for ch in letters.group(1):
        n = n * 26 + (ord(ch) - 64)
    return n - 1


_NS = "{http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/spreadsheetml/2006/main}"
_NS_REL = "{http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships}"
_NS_PACK_REL = "{http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/relationships}"


def dump_stdlib(path: Path) -> None:
    import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

    with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as zf:
        shared: list[str] = []
        if "xl/sharedStrings.xml" in zf.namelist():
            root = ET.fromstring(zf.read("xl/sharedStrings.xml"))
            for si in root.findall(f"{_NS}si"):
                shared.append("".join(t.text or "" for t in si.iter(f"{_NS}t")))

        wb = ET.fromstring(zf.read("xl/workbook.xml"))
        rels = ET.fromstring(zf.read("xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels"))
        target_by_rid = {
            rel.get("Id"): rel.get("Target")
            for rel in rels.findall(f"{_NS_PACK_REL}Relationship")
        }
        for sheet in wb.find(f"{_NS}sheets"):
            title = sheet.get("name") or ""
            rid = sheet.get(f"{_NS_REL}id") or ""
            target = target_by_rid.get(rid, "")
            stripped = target.lstrip("/")
            part = stripped if stripped.startswith("xl/") else "xl/" + stripped
            if part not in zf.namelist():
                print(f"cannot locate sheet part for '{title}': {target}",
                      file=sys.stderr)
                raise KeyError(part)
            ws = ET.fromstring(zf.read(part))
            cells: dict[tuple[int, int], str] = {}
            for c in ws.iter(f"{_NS}c"):
                ref = c.get("r") or ""
                m = re.match(r"([A-Z]+)(\d+)", ref)
                row_n = int(m.group(2)) if m else 0
                col_n = _col_index(ref)
                v = c.find(f"{_NS}v")
                is_node = c.find(f"{_NS}is")
                if is_node is not None:
                    text = "".join(t.text or "" for t in is_node.iter(f"{_NS}t"))
                elif v is not None and v.text is not None:
                    if c.get("t") == "s":
                        idx = int(v.text)
                        text = shared[idx] if idx < len(shared) else v.text
                    else:
                        text = v.text
                else:
                    continue
                if text.strip():
                    cells[(row_n, col_n)] = _clean(text)
            if not cells:
                _print_sheet(title, [])
                continue
            max_row = max(r for r, _ in cells)
            max_col = max(c for _, c in cells)
            rows = [[""] * (max_col + 1) for _ in range(max_row)]
            for (r, c), text in cells.items():
                rows[r - 1][c] = text
            _print_sheet(title, rows)


def main() -> int:
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        print(__doc__.strip().splitlines()[0], file=sys.stderr)
        print("usage: python3 scripts/xlsx_cells.py <file.xlsx>", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    path = Path(sys.argv[1])
    if not path.is_file():
        print(f"not a file: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    if path.suffix.lower() != ".xlsx":
        print(f"not an .xlsx file: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    try:
        try:
            dump_openpyxl(path)
        except ImportError:
            dump_stdlib(path)
    except (zipfile.BadZipFile, KeyError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"cannot read workbook {path}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 3
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# SEC Filing Review (form check / deficiency memo)

You are acting as the reviewing lawyer. In a review memo the asserted
corrections ARE the product: a reviewer whose "correct" values are wrong is
more dangerous than the original draft, because the drafter will apply the
corrections verbatim. Where the task instructions specify structure,
sections, or output files, they control over this skill.

## 1. Memo anatomy

- Privilege legend; To / From / Date / Re (the Re line names the instrument
  reviewed and its date).
- Purpose and scope: what was reviewed (each document with a short name and
  date) and what was NOT reviewed (e.g., execution copies). Findings that
  depend on unreviewed documents say "verify against the execution copy."
- Executive summary: overall conclusion, finding counts by severity, a table
  of the Critical and High findings, and what the review confirmed correct.
- Findings organized by the draft's own architecture (for a Form 8-K, by Item
  number, ascending), then cover page, signature block, and filing mechanics.
- A corrected exhibit index table where exhibits are in issue.
- A consolidated, prioritized action list keyed to finding numbers.
- Assumptions and limitations.

## 2. Finding anatomy

Each finding states: (i) location in the draft; (ii) the draft's language,
quoted or precisely described; (iii) the record value with a short-form cite
to the reviewed document; (iv) why it matters (disclosure standard, filing or
investor consequence); (v) severity; and (vi) the fix — exact replacement
language wherever the record supports it, or an explicit "verify against the
execution copy" where it does not. Never state a "correct" value that no
reviewed document contains.

## 3. Verbatim-source discipline

- Identifiers, amounts, dates, ratios, titles, and names are copied
  character-for-character from the record in both directions: when quoting
  the draft and when stating the correct value. Never paraphrase, round,
  abbreviate, or reconstruct a name or figure from memory.
- Entity names keep their full form, including suffixes (LLC, LP, Inc.,
  P.C.), exactly as the source states them.
- A value that exists only in your working notes — not in a reviewed
  document — is unverified: mark it "verify" or omit it.
- Where sources conflict, report both values and the conflict; never average,
  blend, or silently pick one.
- Cite the specific document and section for every record value a finding
  asserts.

## 4. Verification gate (run before delivering)

Re-open the source documents and check, finding by finding:

1. Every "correct" value in the memo appears verbatim in its cited source.
2. Every quoted "draft" value appears verbatim in the draft.
3. Executive-summary counts and descriptions match the findings body.
4. In any exhibit-index table, the "draft" column is copied from the draft's
   actual index — not from the checklist and not from memory.
5. Every exhibit, schedule, or agreement cited in a finding exists in the
   reviewed documents or is flagged as unreviewed.
6. After generating a binary deliverable, read it back and confirm the
   values — not merely headings, tables, and rendering — against this
   checklist.

A rendering check is not a substantive check. Do not announce verification
until the values pass.

## 5. Severity rubric

- Critical: the filing as drafted is incorrect, incomplete, or misleading
  and must be corrected before filing.
- High: materially deficient; correct before filing absent a documented
  reason not to.
- Medium / Low: accuracy, consistency, or completeness improvements; verify
  or conform.

## 6. Form 8-K finishing checks

- Date of report = date of the EARLIEST event reported, not the latest.
- The cover-page item index must equal the items actually captioned in the
  body; re-check it after adding or re-captioning any item.
- Item mapping: entry into material definitive agreements → Item 1.01 (each
  agreement). Closing of an acquisition → Item 2.01 (caption required even
  if the disclosure is combined with Item 1.01). Borrowings, draws, and
  commitment increases → Item 2.03. Officer departures and appointments →
  Item 5.02 — not Item 5.01, which is change of control. Press releases →
  Item 7.01, furnished, with a furnished-not-filed legend.
- Every unregistered issuance — including placement-agent warrants and
  shares issued as acquisition consideration — → Item 3.02: purchaser
  identities, amounts, exemption basis, absence of general solicitation,
  agent compensation. Calendar the Regulation D Form D (15 days after first
  sale) and the exchange listing-rule analysis.
- Item 9.01(a)/(b): "Not applicable" requires a documented Rule 3-05 /
  Article 11 significance analysis (investment, asset, and income tests;
  20% thresholds, with the 10% income threshold where a registration
  statement is on file). If any test is met, file the required financial
  statements or the 71-day amendment commitment.
- Signature block: name AND title of the signing officer.
- Where a checklist and the draft disagree about an exhibit, verify against
  the draft itself and the deal documents before "correcting" either.

# VC cap table / financing review

Audience: a supervising lawyer who needs an issue inventory, not a summary. For each
material issue: source-cited finding, consequence, severity, practical recommendation.
Keep source text, matter fact, legal inference, risk assessment and recommendation
visibly separate; never present an inference as a quotation.

## Memo anatomy (artifact contract)

Deliver the memo in the file the task names. Expected parts:

1. Executive summary — numbered key findings with dollar/share impact.
2. Transaction overview — parties, round size, price, post-money.
3. Current capitalization vs the charter — every class, charter number vs
   cap-table/term-sheet number, sourced.
4. Corrected economics — FD recomputation on each basis, price per share, new
   shares, post-close table by holder.
5. Term-by-term analysis of proposed terms — preference/stack, anti-dilution,
   board composition, drag-along, pay-to-play.
6. Discrepancy log — EVERY conflicting pair across documents: item, value A
   (source), value B (source), which controls and why, severity.
7. Approvals/consents matrix — action, instrument/section, vote required, parties.
8. Pro-rata / allocation analysis.
9. Recommendations / open items.
10. Appendix — roll-forwards, waterfall, calculation bases.

Parts 3–6 feed 7–8; the discrepancy log must be complete before recommendations
are drafted.

## Analytic moves (in order)

1. Reconcile the charter against every summary document (cap table, term-sheet
   capitalization section, 409A), class by class. Matching aggregates do NOT
   clear the entries: join grant schedules per grant ID (grantee, date, shares,
   price, status) and log every entry-level conflict.
2. Recompute fully diluted capitalization using the round documents' own FD
   definition; apply mandated pre-closing pool increases to the denominator;
   state each basis used.
3. Roll the option pool forward: authorized − granted + forfeited (forfeited
   shares return to the reserve). Pool status is evidenced by the certified plan
   summary and board minutes, not the cap table.
4. Trace every conversion and every forfeiture to its instrument and board-minute
   evidence, with dates.
5. Classify each proposed term; test each protective provision's trigger
   literally against the proposed terms.
6. Compute corrected economics: price, new shares, aggregate liquidation
   preferences, drag threshold, waterfall at representative exit values,
   pro-rata entitlements.
7. Build the consents matrix from the charter, IRA and voting agreement; include
   charter share-authorization capacity as a closing item.

## Decision rules

- Controlling-source hierarchy: charter > certified plan schedules and board
  minutes > executed agreements (note purchase agreement, IRA, voting agreement)
  > term sheet (a proposal, not authority for current facts) > cap table and
  409A (summaries). A charter figure contradicted by a summary is a finding,
  not a judgment call.
- Read triggers literally. A pay-to-play keyed to "any equity financing
  following the closing" of the current round does NOT reach the current round;
  current-round shortfall consequences run through the IRA pro-rata section's
  minimum-participation clause instead. A protective provision covering
  "senior to or on parity with" does not reach a junior series, but a
  per-share-preference trigger applies regardless of ranking.
- Rounding: fractional shares on conversion round down, with cash in lieu,
  per the conversion mechanics.
- Note interest: simple interest, actual days, over the day-count basis stated
  in the note instrument itself; a closing certificate reciting a different
  rate/day-count is a discrepancy to log even when the resulting share count is
  undisputed.
- Charter capacity is a closing condition: post-closing fully diluted (all
  preferred as-converted plus all reserves) vs authorized common.
- In this record the summaries systematically UNDERSTATE real securities (note
  conversion shares, exercised-option common, warrants): when counts conflict,
  the charter-based larger number has controlled; verify it, do not assume it.

import argparse
import itertools
import sys


def parse_named(items, cast=int):
    out = {}
    for item in items:
        name, _, val = item.partition("=")
        out[name] = cast(val)
    return out


def parse_series(spec):
    name, _, rest = spec.partition("=")
    shares, price, mult = rest.split(":")
    return {"name": name, "shares": int(shares), "price": float(price), "mult": float(mult)}


def cmd_fd(a):
    parts = parse_named(a.shares)
    base = sum(parts.values())
    fd = base + a.pool_increase
    for name, val in parts.items():
        print(f"component  {name:<24} {val:>15,}")
    if a.pool_increase:
        print(f"component  {'pool_increase':<24} {a.pool_increase:>15,}")
    print(f"fully_diluted                      {fd:>15,}")
    price = a.pre_money / fd
    print(f"price_per_share                    {price:>15,.6f}")
    if a.investment:
        new_shares = int(a.investment / price)
        cash_left = a.investment - new_shares * price
        print(f"new_shares_for {a.investment:,.2f} {new_shares:>15,}")
        print(f"cash_in_lieu                       {cash_left:>15,.2f}")
        print(f"post_financing_fd                  {fd + new_shares:>15,}")


def cmd_pool(a):
    available = a.authorized - a.granted + a.forfeited
    print(f"authorized {a.authorized:,} - granted {a.granted:,} + forfeited_returned {a.forfeited:,}")
    print(f"available_for_future_grants        {available:>15,}")


def cmd_interest(a):
    interest = a.principal * a.rate * a.days / a.basis
    total = a.principal + interest
    print(f"interest  {a.principal:,.2f} x {a.rate:.4f} x {a.days}/{a.basis} = {interest:,.2f}")
    print(f"total_conversion_or_repayment      {total:>15,.2f}")
    if a.price:
        raw = total / a.price
        whole = int(raw)
        print(f"shares_at_{a.price:<12.4f}          {raw:>15,.4f}")
        print(f"shares_issued_rounded_down         {whole:>15,}")
        print(f"cash_in_lieu                       {total - whole * a.price:>15,.2f}")


def cmd_prorata(a):
    holders = parse_named(a.holder_shares)
    allocations = parse_named(a.allocation, cast=float) if a.allocation else {}
    for name, shares in holders.items():
        pct = shares / a.fd

def payout_at(exit_value, series, choices, common_shares):
    remaining = float(exit_value)
    payouts = {s["name"]: 0.0 for s in series}
    payouts["common"] = 0.0
    for s, choice in zip(series, choices):
        if choice == "pref":
            pref = s["shares"] * s["price"] * s["mult"]
            take = min(pref, remaining)
            payouts[s["name"]] = take
            remaining -= take
    conv_shares = sum(s["shares"] for s, c in zip(series, choices) if c == "convert") + common_shares
    if conv_shares > 0 and remaining > 0:
        for s, choice in zip(series, choices):
            if choice == "convert":
                payouts[s["name"]] += remaining * s["shares"] / conv_shares
        payouts["common"] += remaining * common_shares / conv_shares
    return payouts

    payouts = payout_at(exit_value, series, choices, common_shares)

        flipped[i] = "convert" if choices[i] == "pref" else "pref"
        alt = payout_at(exit_value, series, flipped, common_shares)
        name = series[i]["name"]

# Verify Deliverable

Before declaring any task complete, check the deliverable mechanically.
Reading it again "to make sure it looks right" is not a check: it re-reads
what you already believe. The checks below compare the deliverable against
the *sources*, which is the only comparison that catches substitution
errors (a wrong but plausible name, a figure that matches an earlier draft
instead of the data).

## Procedure

1. **Extract the deliverable text.** Run the workspace document reader on
   the deliverable with host input so the extraction sandbox can see the
   file:

       python3 scripts/read_doc.py <deliverable.docx> --in host

   Capture the full extracted text to a scratch `.txt` file in the
   workspace (never under `/tmp`, which the sandbox forbids).

2. **Check every proper name against the sources.** First extract each
   source document the same way, then run:

       python3 skills/verify-deliverable/scripts/check_entity_drift.py \
         --deliverable MEMO.txt --sources SRC1.txt [SRC2.txt ...]

   The script reports three classes:
   - `PLURAL DRIFT` — the deliverable uses a singular/plural form of a
     source name (e.g. a trade name missing its final "s"). Usually wrong.
   - `MUTATED` — a deliverable name closely resembles a *different*
     source name (swapped first name, drifted company name). Almost always
     a substitution error.
   - `UNSUPPORTED` — a name repeated in the deliverable with no
     counterpart in any source.

   The tool is a filter, not a judge: some lines are heading or list
   fragments. Resolve **every** line before release — for each, either fix
   the deliverable or confirm the deliverable's form against the record.
   Pay special attention to person names and party descriptions: a memo
   that states the wrong declarant, the wrong deponent, or the wrong
   number of named plaintiffs has failed even if every figure in it is
   correct.

3. **Re-verify every figure against the data workbook** by recomputing it
   from the rows with `scripts/verify_greenleaf_headcount.py` (see that
   script's header for usage). Never confirm a figure by finding it
   written somewhere else in the record — summaries and notes can be
   wrong; only the detail rows are ground truth.

4. **Validate the file structure.** For `.docx` output run:

       python3 skills/docx/scripts/validate.py <deliverable.docx>

5. **Reconcile, then report.** Fix the deliverable and re-run the checks
   until the name report is clean and every figure conflict is explained.
   Only then declare the task complete, and say in the completion message
   which checks were run — not just that "all verification steps pass."

# Reviewing a tax document against the matter record

The baseline document (the memo, agreement, or return under review) is checked
against the supporting documents (agreement excerpts, diligence reports,
valuation workpapers, capitalization records, correspondence). Three rules
govern every finding. Each is a check to perform before the finding ships, not
background reading.

## 1. A secondary source's claim about the baseline document is itself a reviewable claim

Diligence and valuation sources assert what the baseline document "omits",
"includes", or "fails to address". Never adopt such a characterization as your
own finding.

- Before reporting "X omits/contains Y" on source Z's say-so, read X's actual
  itemization of that section and recompute the variance from the line items
  both documents state. A variance is confirmed only when you can name the
  lines that produce it; adjectives in a diligence note are not confirmation.
- If Z's characterization turns out wrong, the error is itself a finding:
  report it with pin cites to both Z and X.

## 2. Reconcile every population, count, and date across documents

Counts of holders, parties, agreements, filings, or dates of the same event
made by different documents in the same matter routinely conflict. Each
conflict is a finding, not a tie to break silently.

- Enumerate each population from its primary record (e.g., the cap-table
  detail rows), then compare every other document's stated count against it -
  including totals and summary rows, which are often inconsistent with their
  own detail.
- Where documents disagree, report every version with its source; agreement
  among secondary documents never overrides the primary record.
- A summary row's arithmetic must match the detail it summarizes; when it
  does not, name the entries that make it fail.

## 3. Trace cross-cutting provisions through the whole instrument

Eligibility, consent, change-of-control, transfer-restriction, and
tax-treatment provisions rarely appear in only one place in an operative
agreement.

- Once such a provision bears on a finding, search the instrument's full text
  (definitions, representations, covenants, closing conditions, schedules) and
  cite every section that states, repeats, or contradicts it. Finding one
  section that says it is not finding what the agreement says.
- If two provisions of the same instrument state the concept differently,
  report the internal conflict; do not pick one silently.

# Adoption consent drafting — practitioner model

You are producing a court-filed instrument plus advice to a supervising lawyer.
Own the legal deliverable, not just text: whose consent, which proceeding,
which statute, what the instrument may and may not lawfully do, and what the
supervising lawyer must be told. File formats, validation and output routing
belong to the harness; this skill governs legal content only.

## 1. Confirm the instrument before drafting

- One instrument per consenting parent. Recite that the other parent's consent
  is separate and that this consent is independently required.
- Caption in the adoption case, never the guardianship or support case (see
  the case join under Verified workspace facts).
- Identify the statute the sources cite for the proceeding, then verify
  subtitle and section numbers against current primary law (annotated code,
  court rules, or an authorised research path) before any operative clause
  depends on them. Citations appearing in intake memos, reports, and counsel
  letters are unverified until confirmed.
- Confirm whose client the consenting parent is and that their counsel is
  independent of the petitioners (independently retained and paid).

## 2. Decision rule — "make the consent final and irrevocable immediately"

Trigger: a party or client asks for the consent to be irrevocable on signing,
with no waiting period.

1. Locate the controlling withdrawal/revocation provision and record, with a
   source: (a) the window's length; (b) its start events (date of execution;
   any counsel-appointment trigger); (c) whether the statute's own text permits
   waiving the right inside the consent; (d) whether execution before a judge
   or magistrate changes revocability.
2. Only verified propositions become operative recitals. If waivability is not
   established from primary material or an authorised research path, do NOT
   draft an express-waiver clause as the mechanism delivering immediate
   irrevocability, and do NOT tell the supervising lawyer that this is how the
   wish "can lawfully be implemented." Draft instead: disclosure of the
   withdrawal right as far as verified; a memo statement of what cannot be
   promised and why; and the lawful alternatives — prompt filing and service;
   execution in court if that is verified to matter; calendaring finalization
   after the window runs (never schedule the finalization hearing inside an
   unwaived withdrawal window unless verified law permits it).
3. Consistency check before finishing: no operative clause may assert as
   settled law a proposition that another section of the deliverables lists as
   "to verify." Hedging in a later section does not cure an unverified
   operative recital.

Failure this rule prevents (observed in this workspace's base run): the
consent recited that the statutory revocation right exists "unless the right
of revocation is expressly waived in the consent itself," and the memo
presented the express waiver as the lawful route to the mother's wish — while
the same memo's legal-framework section said to confirm the
revocation/waiver provision. Nothing in the record establishes the period's
length, start events, or waivability. An invalid waiver clause invites a
post-placement collateral attack — the most expensive failure in this work.

## 3. Decision rule — post-adoption contact / visitation

Trigger: any question whether a contact arrangement belongs "in the adoption
papers" or in the consent.

- Keep the consent unconditional. A consent conditioned on promised future
  contact is vulnerable to invalidation for inducement or condition.
- Verify this jurisdiction's treatment of post-adoption contact agreements
  from primary material before advising; do not assert enforceability OR
  non-enforceability without a source.
- If the understanding is documented at all, it goes in a separate instrument
  whose binding effect is stated expressly per verified law; recommend
  coordinating with the consenting parent's counsel.
- Check whether an existing guardianship order grants contact rights; those
  end with the adoption — say so in the memo.
- The memo must answer the actual question asked in the record (who asked,
  in which document), including any invitation to coordinate with the other
  side's counsel.

## 4. Consent — required parts (check each)

Caption block: court, adoption caption, adoption case number, instrument title
naming the consenting parent.

Recitals, in order: (1) consenting parent identified — name, date of birth,
address, adult status, relationship to the child; (2) child identified — name,
date of birth, place of birth, birth-certificate number; no Social Security
number or other unnecessary identifier; (3) adoptive parents identified,
including each one's relationship to the child and to each other; (4) pending
proceeding — petition, case number, judge, and the live guardianship order by
case number; (5) the other parent's separate consent recited with its
execution details as known, expressly not a substitute for this one; (6)
independent counsel — name, firm, address, retained and paid solely by the
consenting parent; advice on rights including withdrawal; receipt of an
executed copy; (7) consequences in plain language — which rights end (custody,
visitation and contact, decision-making), who the legal parents become, that
the effect is permanent; (8) voluntariness, no coercion, no payment or
inducement by anyone, and capacity — with known history (e.g., treatment and
recovery) affirmatively disclosed rather than omitted; (9) the withdrawal
right handled per §2; (10) consent to adoption by the named petitioners and
request for the decree; any notice waiver only "to the extent permitted by
law"; (11) an unconditionality clause per §3; (12) verification/declaration
of truthfulness.

Execution apparatus: execution date line; consenting parent's signature block
with name and address; counsel approval/certificate block; two disinterested
witnesses; a notary acknowledgment block WITH an alternative for execution
before a judge, magistrate, or other officer authorised by statute to take
consents — and resolve from the statute, before the signing is scheduled,
which officers the law actually authorises.

## 5. Drafting memorandum — required parts (check each)

(1) TO/FROM/DATE/RE, privilege line, matter number. (2) Assignment in one
paragraph, including the family map stated correctly in plain words — e.g.
"petitioner X is the child's paternal aunt, sister of the biological father;
the consenting mother and the father were never married" — then check each
clause of that sentence against the court order's findings before finishing
(the base run here opened with a garbled "clients' sister-in-law's
co-parent"). (3) Numbered recommendations, each traceable to a source or
flagged as inference. (4) Parties/counsel/proceedings table with sources.
(5) Source-document list. (6) Drafting decisions keyed to the consent's
paragraphs. (7) A discrepancy log — one row per conflict: number, conflict,
treatment adopted, follow-up — covering every conflict found however small,
plus a list of key identifiers verified consistent. (8) Legal framework
separating verified citations from to-verify items at the point of use.
(9) Execution logistics — officer identity, attendees (the consenting
parent's counsel present so the certificate is contemporaneous), when the
draft goes to that counsel (calendar any review window they asked for), what
gets filed afterward. (10) Open items with owners and dates. (11) Limitations.

Separation discipline throughout: label what is source text, matter fact,
legal inference, risk assessment, and recommendation — never present one as
another.

## 6. Discrepancy handling

Hierarchy for identity data (names, dates of birth, identifiers, case
numbers): court-order findings > executed or notarized instruments and counsel
confirmations > professional reports (home studies) > intake memoranda >
informal email recitals. Corroborate the winning value independently (e.g.,
certificate-number year against date of birth; stated age or school grade
against date of birth; arithmetic of ages against stated dates). Every
conflict is logged even when resolved, and a resolved conflict still gets a
follow-up (obtain the certified record; correct the internal file).

Treat counsel's legal characterisations as advocacy, not law. A claim that a
parent's relinquishment "resolves all obligations related to the child" does
not by itself extinguish accrued support arrearages: check whether the
existing support order is expressly preserved by a court order, and whether
public-assistance benefits paid during part of the arrears period (e.g., TANF)
create an assigned State claim for the overlap.

- `edit` calls against the same file must be sequential. Several edits to one
  file issued in a single turn race: all but the last are silently lost even
  though each reports success. After a batch of edits, re-check the file for
  the intended changes rather than trusting the per-call confirmations.
